messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Your doctor will use blood tests to check that your dose is right, usually 6 to 8 weeks after any dose change, and then every 6 to 12 months once your dose is stable. Children are tested more often, including 2 and 4 weeks after starting treatment and 2 weeks after any dose change.
Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you take biotin, or a multivitamin, hair, skin, or nail supplement that contains biotin (sometimes listed as vitamin B7). Biotin can interfere with thyroid blood tests and give a falsely high or falsely low result, which could lead to the wrong dose change. Stop biotin and any biotin-containing supplements at least 2 days before a thyroid blood test.
If your symptoms and blood tests still suggest an underactive thyroid even though you are on a dose that should be enough, it may be because the medicine is not being absorbed properly, doses are being missed, or another medicine is interfering. Talk to your doctor before your dose is increased.

The relation 'has possible reason for ineffective treatment' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug may not be effective due to the reason specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has reduced efficacy in': The subject drug may be less effective in patients with the condition or factor specified by the object entity.
B. 'has maximum dose': The subject drug should not exceed the maximum dose specified by the object entity.
C. 'has off label use': The subject drug is used for purposes not specifically approved or listed in the official medication guide, as specified by the object entity.
D. 'reduces response to': The subject drug may decrease the effectiveness or response to the object entity.
E. 'has side effect': The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
